title: First as Tragedy? Second as What? Estimating Dynamic Effects of Recurrent Events
abstract: arXiv:2609.30007v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: I study treatment effect estimation when treatment events have persistent effects and can be experienced more than once. Natural disasters, job loss and health shocks are examples of such treatments. I show that the effect of a total treatment trajectory can be recovered under assumptions similar to those commonly invoked in single-event settings using suitably flexible TWFE models. Decomposing the total trajectory effect into portions attributable to distinct event occurrences, however, requires further assumptions. I propose an assumption similar to conditional parallel trends, imposing it on the growth of event-specific effects rather than on untreated outcomes. Combined with a linear-in-parameters model of effect growth, this assumption enables a sequential imputation estimator that consistently estimates the dynamic effects of each event occurrence and that can accommodate heterogeneity in effects according to observable event attri

translated_title: 第一次是悲剧？第二次又是什么？——估计重复事件的动态效应
translated_abstract: 本文研究当处理事件具有持续效应且可能被多次经历时的处理效应估计问题，自然灾害、失业和健康冲击都属于这类处理。我证明，在与单次事件设定中常用假设相近的条件下，利用足够灵活的双向固定效应（TWFE）模型，可以恢复总处理轨迹的效应。然而，若要将总轨迹效应分解为可归因于各次事件发生的部分，则需要额外的假设。我提出了一个类似于条件平行趋势的假设，但将其施加于事件特定效应的增长之上，而非未处理的结果之上。结合效应增长的线性参数模型，该假设使得序贯插补估计量成为可能，该估计量能够一致地估计每次事件发生的动态效应，并可以根据可观测的事件属性来容纳效应的异质性。
tldr: 本文提出在“事件特定效应增长”上施加类条件平行趋势假设，并结合线性效应增长模型构造序贯插补估计量，从而能够一致地识别和估计重复事件（如灾害、失业、健康冲击）中每次事件发生的动态处理效应及其异质性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a sequential imputation estimator, based on a conditional-parallel-trends-like assumption imposed on event-specific effect growth, that consistently recovers the dynamic effects of each occurrence of recurrent events (e.g., disasters, job loss, health shocks) and accommodates effect heterogeneity.
